items.text:
11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

One afternoon Nila was returning from the market when she noticed a wallet beside a fruit stall. She picked it up and wondered what to do next.
items.explanation:
Sample title: A wallet near the market

One afternoon Nila was returning from the market when she noticed a wallet beside a fruit stall. She picked it up and wondered what to do next. She asked the stallkeeper whether he had seen anyone drop it. He had not noticed its owner. Nila opened the wallet only to look for identification. She found a card with a name but no telephone number. The stallkeeper suggested taking it to the nearby police desk. Nila agreed and gave the wallet to an officer. The officer recorded where she had found it. Later, a worried woman came to report a missing wallet. After checking her identity, the officer returned it to her. The woman thanked Nila for her honesty. Nila went home happy that the wallet was safely returned.

items.text:
11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

A group of students wanted to grow vegetables behind their school. At first, they worked eagerly, but after a few weeks they stopped visiting the garden.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The neglected garden

A group of students wanted to grow vegetables behind their school. At first, they worked eagerly, but after a few weeks they stopped visiting the garden. One morning they found weeds growing around the young plants. Some leaves were drooping in the dry soil. The students realised that their plan needed regular care. They met their teacher and asked for advice. She encouraged them to share the work fairly. Together they made a weekly watering and weeding schedule. Each small team took responsibility for one day. They also collected rainwater in a covered container. After several weeks, the plants began to grow well again. The students harvested a few vegetables and shared them with the school cook. They learned that a good beginning must be followed by steady effort.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

On her way to school, Rupa saw that the small wooden bridge over a narrow ditch had been damaged by rain. Several younger children were waiting on the other side.
items.explanation:
Sample title: A broken bridge

On her way to school, Rupa saw that the small wooden bridge over a narrow ditch had been damaged by rain. Several younger children were waiting on the other side. Rupa told the children not to step onto the broken boards. She remembered a longer path that crossed the ditch at a safe culvert. She asked an adult nearby to accompany the group. Together they walked along the longer route to school. After arriving, Rupa informed the headteacher about the bridge. The headteacher contacted local residents and the relevant authorities. They placed a warning sign near the damaged crossing. A repair team inspected the bridge and replaced the unsafe boards. The adults checked the bridge before allowing children to use it again. The children were relieved to have a safe route. Rupa learned the value of careful action and asking adults for help.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

After school, Arif discovered a notebook on a bench at the bus stop. He noticed a name on its cover, but he did not know the owner.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Lost Notebook

After school, Arif discovered a notebook on a bench at the bus stop. He noticed a name on its cover, but he did not know the owner. He took the notebook to the school office. The clerk recognised the name as that of a student from another class. She contacted the class teacher. The teacher asked her students about the notebook. Soon the owner came to the office. She explained that she had left it while waiting for the bus. The clerk asked her to describe its cover. The description matched the notebook. She returned it to the relieved student. The student thanked Arif the next day. Arif was glad that he had taken the notebook to a safe place.

items.text:
11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

Mitu promised her grandmother that she would visit her on Friday. On that morning, her friends invited her to a football match.
items.explanation:
Sample title: A Promise Kept

Mitu promised her grandmother that she would visit her on Friday. On that morning, her friends invited her to a football match. Mitu wanted to watch the match very much. Then she remembered her promise. She explained the situation to her friends. They suggested that she visit her grandmother first. Mitu took some fruit and went to her grandmother’s house. Her grandmother was delighted to see her. They talked about the old days and shared the fruit. Mitu helped her arrange some books on a low shelf. When it was time to leave, her grandmother thanked her. Mitu reached the field before the second half began. She enjoyed both the visit and the game.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

Tanvir left home late on the day of a school exhibition. When he reached the bus stop, the bus had already gone.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Missed Bus

Tanvir left home late on the day of a school exhibition. When he reached the bus stop, the bus had already gone. He felt worried because his model was needed at the exhibition. He called his teacher to explain the delay. The teacher told him to travel safely rather than rush. Tanvir checked the time of the next bus. It was due in fifteen minutes. He waited with his model protected inside a bag. When the bus arrived, he found a seat near the front. He reached school shortly after the exhibition began. His classmates had kept a space ready for his model. Tanvir set it up and explained it to the visitors. Afterwards, he decided to leave earlier for important events.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

For weeks, Lata and her friends had planned a picnic in the park. On the chosen morning, heavy rain began to fall.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Rainy-Day Plan

For weeks, Lata and her friends had planned a picnic in the park. On the chosen morning, heavy rain began to fall. The children were disappointed at first. Their teacher reminded them not to travel through flooded streets. They decided to postpone the picnic. Instead, each student prepared something at home for a later class meeting. Lata drew a picture of the park. One friend wrote a short poem about rain. Another made a list of games for the next sunny day. The teacher collected their ideas when school reopened. A week later, the weather improved. The class enjoyed the picnic safely. Their preparation made the new plan even more enjoyable.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

Sadia found several extra bean seeds after planting her small garden. She wondered whether her neighbours could use them.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Seed Exchange

Sadia found several extra bean seeds after planting her small garden. She wondered whether her neighbours could use them. She put the seeds in clean paper packets. On each packet she wrote the name of the plant. She asked her mother to help her speak to the neighbours. Several families were interested in growing beans. One neighbour offered tomato seeds in exchange. Another shared advice about watering seedlings. Sadia planted a few tomato seeds in a pot. The neighbours compared their plants as they grew. When a seedling looked weak, they discussed what it needed. Soon the lane had several small gardens. Sadia learned that sharing resources can bring people together.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

During a class game, Rafi accidentally knocked over his friend’s water bottle. The water spilled across a poster they had made together.
items.explanation:
Sample title: A Careful Apology

During a class game, Rafi accidentally knocked over his friend’s water bottle. The water spilled across a poster they had made together. Rafi quickly moved the bottle away from the poster. His friend looked upset because the colours had run. Rafi admitted that he had been careless. He apologised without blaming anyone else. Together they lifted the poster onto a dry table. Their teacher brought paper towels to absorb the water. The picture could not be restored completely. Rafi offered to help make a new one. His friend agreed and suggested a simpler design. They worked together after class and finished it the next day. Their honest conversation helped protect their friendship.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

The clock in the school library stopped one afternoon. Students began arriving late for their next lessons because they trusted its hands.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Library Clock

The clock in the school library stopped one afternoon. Students began arriving late for their next lessons because they trusted its hands. The librarian checked the battery first. She found that it had run out. She told the students that the clock was not working. A student wrote a temporary notice and placed it nearby. The librarian obtained a new battery from the office. Together with a staff member, she replaced the old one. They set the hands using a reliable clock. The next morning they checked that it still kept the correct time. The librarian removed the warning notice. She thanked the students for reporting the problem. Everyone returned to reading without worrying about a misleading clock.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

Nabil was waiting outside school when a sudden shower began. He had an umbrella, but his neighbour Joya had none.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Shared Umbrella

Nabil was waiting outside school when a sudden shower began. He had an umbrella, but his neighbour Joya had none. Joya’s home was on the same street as Nabil’s. He offered to share the umbrella. They waited until the heaviest rain had passed. Then they walked slowly along the pavement. At a busy road, they stopped and used the marked crossing. The umbrella was small, so they stayed close together. When the wind grew stronger, they sheltered beside a shop. The shopkeeper told them a drain ahead had overflowed. They chose a safer route around it. Soon they reached Joya’s gate. Joya thanked Nabil, who then continued home.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

A new student named Farhan joined Class Eight in the middle of the term. During the first break, he sat alone at his desk.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Quiet New Student

A new student named Farhan joined Class Eight in the middle of the term. During the first break, he sat alone at his desk. A classmate named Rima noticed that he looked uncertain. She introduced herself and asked if he wanted to join her group. Farhan agreed, although he spoke quietly at first. The group showed him the library and the playground. They explained the timetable and the rules of their classroom. At lunch, Farhan shared a story about his old school. The others listened with interest. In a later lesson, he offered an idea for a group poster. His classmates included it in their design. By the end of the week, Farhan felt more comfortable. Rima learned that a simple invitation can help someone feel welcome.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

The students noticed that a tap in the school washroom kept dripping. Every day a small pool of water formed underneath it.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Leaking Tap

The students noticed that a tap in the school washroom kept dripping. Every day a small pool of water formed underneath it. They told their class teacher about the leak. She asked the caretaker to inspect the tap. The caretaker placed a bucket underneath while waiting for a repair. The students used the collected water for cleaning where appropriate. The headteacher arranged for a plumber to visit. The plumber replaced a worn part inside the tap. He checked that the tap closed properly. The students cleared the floor so no one would slip. Their teacher discussed why leaks should be reported early. The class made a reminder about turning taps off carefully. The small repair prevented further waste.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

Jerin entered a school drawing competition but did not win a prize. She folded her picture and said she would never draw again.
items.explanation:
Sample title: A Second Attempt

Jerin entered a school drawing competition but did not win a prize. She folded her picture and said she would never draw again. Her art teacher asked her what she liked about the picture. Jerin pointed to the colours in the sky. The teacher agreed that the colours were lively. She also suggested practising the shapes of trees. Jerin took the advice home. She spent a little time drawing different trees each week. Her younger brother offered to be her audience. Later, she entered another school activity. This time she enjoyed explaining how she had improved. Whether or not she won, she felt proud of her effort. She discovered that one disappointment need not end a favourite hobby.

items.text:
11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

A notice about a neighbourhood clean-up appeared on the school board. Many students wanted to join, but they did not know what to bring.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Community Notice

A notice about a neighbourhood clean-up appeared on the school board. Many students wanted to join, but they did not know what to bring. Their teacher contacted the organisers for details. The organisers asked volunteers to bring gloves and reusable water bottles. They also explained that adults would supervise the work. The students wrote the information on the class board. On the appointed morning, they met the adults at the community centre. The organisers divided them into small groups. Each group collected litter from a safe area. Sharp or dangerous objects were left for the adults to handle. The volunteers sorted the collected waste as instructed. They washed their hands after the work. The cleaner surroundings encouraged them to keep the area tidy.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

Sohan borrowed a storybook from his friend Anika. One evening, he noticed that a page had come loose.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Borrowed Book

Sohan borrowed a storybook from his friend Anika. One evening, he noticed that a page had come loose. He remembered that the book belonged to Anika. He decided not to hide the damage. The next day he showed her the loose page and apologised. Anika appreciated his honesty but felt disappointed. They asked the school librarian how to handle the book. The librarian advised them not to use ordinary adhesive tape. She showed them how to keep the page safely inside a protective envelope. Sohan offered to help arrange a proper repair. With an adult’s help, they took the book to a local bookbinder. The bookbinder repaired the page. Sohan returned the book and thanked Anika for lending it.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

The class was preparing a short play for an assembly. On rehearsal day, the student playing the narrator lost her voice.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Small Stage

The class was preparing a short play for an assembly. On rehearsal day, the student playing the narrator lost her voice. She told the teacher that she could not speak loudly. The teacher advised her to rest rather than strain her voice. The group discussed how to continue the rehearsal. Another student offered to read the narrator’s lines. The original narrator followed the script silently and helped with cues. The actors adjusted their movements to the new reader. At first, they missed several signals. They practised again and agreed on clear hand gestures. On assembly day, the narrator’s voice had improved. She and the substitute shared the reading. The play went well because everyone supported the change.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

After the final lesson, Rina could not find her lunchbox. She remembered placing it near the classroom window.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Missing Lunchbox

After the final lesson, Rina could not find her lunchbox. She remembered placing it near the classroom window. She checked her bag and the shelf under her desk. The lunchbox was not there. Her friend suggested asking the class monitor. The monitor had seen a similar box in the corridor. They went to the corridor together but found only a water bottle. A cleaner told them that a lunchbox had been taken to the office. Rina went there with her friend. She described its colour and the sticker on its lid. The office assistant checked the description and returned it. Rina thanked the cleaner and the assistant. She wrote her name on the box so it would be easier to identify.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

During a quiz, Imran gave an answer that made several classmates laugh. He became embarrassed and stopped raising his hand.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Wrong Answer

During a quiz, Imran gave an answer that made several classmates laugh. He became embarrassed and stopped raising his hand. The teacher reminded the class that mistakes are part of learning. She asked Imran to explain how he had reached his answer. He described the first step of his reasoning. The teacher showed him where the calculation had changed. Together they worked through the problem on the board. His classmates saw that the first step had been correct. One student apologised for laughing. Imran tried a similar question at home. The next day he volunteered an answer again. This time his reasoning led to the correct result. He felt more confident because he had learned from the mistake.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

A crowd gathered at the ferry terminal after a long delay. A young boy became separated from his family among the waiting passengers.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Ferry Queue

A crowd gathered at the ferry terminal after a long delay. A young boy became separated from his family among the waiting passengers. A shopkeeper noticed the boy looking worried. She asked him to stay beside her stall. She informed a terminal official about the situation. The official made an announcement describing where the boy could be found. The boy remembered his mother’s name and shared it with the official. Soon a woman approached the stall. She spoke to the official and identified her son. The boy recognised her and ran to her. The official checked that they were travelling together. The mother thanked the shopkeeper for helping safely. The family then joined the queue together.

items.text:
11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

The students had two ideas for a wall magazine: a nature issue and a sports issue. Both groups wanted their idea to be chosen.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Class Vote

The students had two ideas for a wall magazine: a nature issue and a sports issue. Both groups wanted their idea to be chosen. Their teacher suggested that each group explain its plan. The nature group proposed articles about local trees. The sports group suggested reports on school games. Other students asked questions about both plans. The class then held a secret vote. The nature issue received more votes. The sports group was disappointed but accepted the result. The teacher suggested making sports the theme of the next issue. Everyone helped collect and edit material for the first magazine. The finished pages included drawings, poems and short reports. The students learned that listening and fair voting can settle a disagreement.

items.text:
11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

Tisha’s bicycle chain came off while she was riding near home. She stopped safely beside the road and looked at it.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Repaired Bicycle

Tisha’s bicycle chain came off while she was riding near home. She stopped safely beside the road and looked at it. She knew that she should not continue riding with a loose chain. She called her father and explained where she was. He came with a neighbour who understood bicycle repairs. They walked the bicycle to a nearby repair shop. The mechanic checked the chain and gears. He found that the chain needed adjustment. He put it back and tested the pedals. He also checked the brakes and tyres. Tisha watched and asked how to notice a problem early. The mechanic explained some basic safety checks. Tisha thanked him and rode home only after the bicycle had been checked.

items.text:
11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

The school club received a box of coloured paper for a group project. When the box was opened, there was less paper than the students expected.
items.explanation:
Sample title: A Fair Share

The school club received a box of coloured paper for a group project. When the box was opened, there was less paper than the students expected. Several students reached for their favourite colours. Their leader asked everyone to pause and count the sheets. The group listed the materials each team needed. They discovered that some teams could use both sides of a sheet. Others agreed to combine smaller pieces into a collage. The leader divided the remaining paper as fairly as possible. A teacher gave them some clean scrap paper for practice. The teams avoided cutting the best sheets until their designs were ready. By the end of the session, every team had completed its work. A few unused sheets were saved for another day. The students saw that planning could make limited resources go further.
